Which DC Comics limited series, originally published as twelve issues in 1986–1987, is widely regarded as one of the greatest superhero comics ever made?
questions.explanation: Watchmen was written by Alan Moore and illustrated by Dave Gibbons, published by DC Comics as a twelve-issue limited series from 1986 to 1987. It was later collected into a single graphic novel and remains one of the most acclaimed and influential works in comic book history. Time magazine even named it one of the 100 best English-language novels of the 20th century.

questions.question: Which Marvel superhero team did Jack Kirby co-create, helping launch the publisher's modern era?
questions.explanation: Jack Kirby and Stan Lee co-created The Fantastic Four in 1961, a landmark moment that kicked off Marvel's Silver Age of comics. The team — Mr. Fantastic, the Invisible Woman, the Human Torch, and the Thing — introduced a more human, flawed style of superhero storytelling. Kirby's dynamic visual style became a defining influence on the entire Marvel universe.

questions.question: The Harvey Awards, given annually for excellence in comics, are named in honor of which writer-artist?
questions.explanation: The Harvey Awards are named after Harvey Kurtzman, the legendary writer and artist best known for founding Mad Magazine in 1952. Kurtzman's satirical genius and influence on American comics culture made him a fitting namesake for one of the industry's most prestigious honors. The awards have been presented annually since 1988.

questions.question: According to Collider, the Chainsaw Man film adaptation set for a worldwide theatrical release on October 24, 2025 — despite surrounding criticism — is based on which arc from Tatsuki Fujimoto's original manga series?
questions.explanation: Chainsaw Man: The Movie — Reze Arc was announced to open in Japanese theaters on September 24, 2025, followed by a worldwide release on October 24, 2025, despite criticism from some fans. The film adapts the "Bomb Girl" storyline from Tatsuki Fujimoto's manga, which centers on the mysterious Reze and her connection to Denji. By rooting the question in Fujimoto's original manga source material, it firmly belongs in the Entertainment: Comics category.
